_note: Blender job kinds (DECISIONS B74, docs/BLENDER-PIPELINE.md 'Jobs'). A job is {model, steps: [{kind, ...params}]} run by tools/blender/jobs.mjs on the shipped model in client/assets/slice/models/. Each kind lists its params: type int|number|bool|string|strings|map|color, with min/max (numbers, list lengths, string lengths) and req. targets: which models it applies to (character = a rigged model folder, prop = props/<name>.glb). A new kind is an entry here plus its handler in jobs.mjs (KIND_RUN).

inspect.what: Print the model: triangles, materials, textures, size, clips (length), bones (parent, rest position in Blender's Z-up armature space, how many vertices each bone moves, the lowest of them). Changes nothing; read it before writing a recipe.

library.what: List the free animation library's clips (Quaternius Universal Animation Library, CC0) with their lengths. Changes nothing.

motion.what: Make walk, run and idle cycles (and overlays on existing clips) from the model's recipe tools/blender/recipes/<model>.json: feet planted by construction, for four-legged, many-legged and winged bodies. Without clips, every clip and overlay in the recipe.

rigfix.what: Add bones from the recipe's rigfix section and move the mesh's weights onto them (legs the rig lacks, a tail, wings). Every clip the model has keeps playing; the new bones rest until a motion step moves them.

retarget.what: Put library clips on a two-legged model that has the shared Tripo biped skeleton: clips maps a library clip to {name, loop, sequence (library clips joined in order), inPlace, trim ([from s, to s]), speed (0.25 to 4)}. Record the clip's row in docs/ANIMATION-SOURCES.md when it ships.

cleanup.what: Fix one clip in place: loop closes the seam, drift removes the body sliding away over the clip, footLock pins feet while they touch the ground (one contact per foot per cycle).

clips.what: Rename clips (rename: {old: new}) or drop clips (drop: [names]). The model's rows follow.

recolor.what: Shift the colour texture: hue (degrees), saturation and brightness (multipliers). only: {color: '#rrggbb', within: 0.05-1} limits it to texels near that colour (soft edge).

decimate.what: Reduce the mesh to about this many triangles (Blender's collapse decimation; skin weights and UVs are kept).

reshape.what: Grow or shrink the part of the mesh a bone moves (and, with children, the bones below it), around the bone's head: a bigger head, longer horns, smaller claws. Best on ends of the body; scale 0.5 to 2.

remove.what: Delete the faces these bones (and, with children, the bones below them) move most: a tail, a horn, a cape. The bones stay.
